hero.eyebrow: For lecturers and their students · English & français
hero.body: Clasync is for lecturers who teach several classes, sometimes at more than one school. You put a code on the projector and students check in from their phones. Assignments, submissions and marks live in the same place.

projector.label: Example: the check-in code on a classroom projector
projector.enterCode: Enter this code · Entrez ce code

phone.label: Example: a student checking in on a phone
phone.caption: On the student's own phone.

attendance.label: Attendance
attendance.before: A sheet passed round the room, then a headcount to catch names written in for friends who stayed home.
attendance.after: A code on the projector that changes every minute, and a count you can check against the room.

assignments.label: Assignments
assignments.before: Work given out loud and forgotten by the next class.
assignments.after: Each assignment is written down and emailed to every student. Anyone who hasn't handed it in gets a reminder the day before.

marks.label: Marks
marks.before: One Excel file per class, kept up to date by hand.
marks.after: Submissions, marks and comments sit together. Students see their mark when you release it.

attendance.title: A code that changes every minute
attendance.body: You put the code on the projector and students type it on their phones. It changes every 60 seconds, so checking in for a friend who isn't there is a lot harder than writing their name on a sheet.

points.twoCheckIns: Two check-ins, at the start and the end of class. Students who do both are marked present.
points.liveCount: A live count you can compare with the heads in the room.
points.campus: If you turn it on, students have to be on campus to check in.
points.corrections: You can change any mark by hand, and Clasync notes who changed it.

example.label: Example: attendance history for a course

assignments.title: Work nobody forgets
assignments.body: Every assignment goes out by email. The day before it's due, Clasync reminds the students who haven't handed anything in.

points.formats: Students can type an answer, upload a file or send a photo of a handwritten page.
points.late: You decide whether late work is accepted. If it is, you see how late each one was.
points.release: You mark one submission at a time, then release all the grades together.
points.private: Students only ever see their own mark.

schools.title: Several schools, one account
schools.body: Every class you teach is on one dashboard, grouped by school.

shared.title: One class list, shared
shared.body: Colleagues who teach the same class share its student list. They never see your attendance or your marks.

languages.title: English and French
languages.body: Everyone picks their language, and the emails they get follow it.

data.title: Light on data
data.body: There's nothing to install. Photos are shrunk before they upload, and a half-written answer stays on the phone if the connection drops.

school.title: Add your school and class
school.body: Search for your school first. A colleague may have added it already.

code.title: Share the student code
code.body: Post it in the class WhatsApp group. Each student joins once with their matricule.

checkIn.title: Start a check-in
checkIn.body: Put the code on the projector and watch the count go up.

ca.title: CA marks
ca.body: Worked out from attendance, assignments and tests.

tests.title: Tests in class
tests.body: Timed, and opened only when you say so.

notes.title: Notes and revision
notes.body: Course material and practice questions, by topic.

assistant.title: Your own AI assistant
assistant.body: Connected over MCP. Anything it writes waits for your approval.
